title: SSO/SAML ⇄ Customer HSM Integration: Delegated Key Custody, RBAC Drift Remediation & Audit Acceptance Playbook
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Purpose: Produce an executable acceptance playbook and sign-off checklist for integrations where customers bring their own HSM/KMS and federate identity via SSO/SAML. Scope includes delegated key custody flows, RBAC binding and drift detection, audit-log schema & retention requirements, operator procedures for upgrade/rotation, and a minimal evidence package for enterprise sign-off. Excludes: full HSM appliance provisioning (handled by ops), non-SAML identity providers that do not support SAML 2.0 assertions.
acceptance_criteria: SSO/SAML federation: successful end-to-end login test documented with assertion traces and SAML metadata exchange captured in evidence package
Delegated key custody: customer HSM key import, key usage (sign/decrypt), and backup/escrow proof recorded; cryptographic operations verified by sample signing artifacts
RBAC bindings: at least three role bindings (admin/operator/viewer) exercised end-to-end; automated drift detection rule fires when a manual role change diverges from canonical mapping

Audit logging: audit events for authn/authz, key operations, operator actions, and critical config changes are emitted to the customer's audited endpoint with defined schema (timestamp, actor, actor_id, action, resource, request_id, old_value, new_value)
Evidence package: Confluence checklist, logs (redacted), SAML traces, HSM operation records, GitHub PR linking infra changes, and signed attestation from the on-call engineer
Upgrade/rotation plan: documented rollback and live rotation smoke tests validated in a staging tenant with no data-loss and <5% request error increase during controlled rotation
checklist: 1) Preflight: confirm customer SAML metadata, assertion format (NameID/email), and endpoints
2) KMS handshake: exchange public key material and validate key identifiers (kid) via test sign operation
3) RBAC mapping: deploy canonical mapping CR and run mapping smoke script; capture mapping diff report
4) Audit sink: configure and validate audit forwarder; confirm schema conformance and retention policy
5) Operator playbook: run simulated operator upgrade that rotates signing key and observe KV cache continuity
6) Evidence assembly: collect logs, SAML traces, PRs, and a one-paragraph attestation from security reviewer
7) Sign-off: security, product, and infra leads sign acceptance PDF and attach to ticket
risks: SAML assertion attribute mismatch causing silent auth failures for multi-tenant customers
HSM vendor-specific behavior (e.g., slot limitations) causing partial feature availability
RBAC drift not detected quickly enough if audit logs are delayed or lost
Operator key rotation can cause transient cache invalidation that impacts latency-sensitive customers
decisions: Decision 2025-02-18: Require SAML 2.0 metadata exchange and valid x509 signing cert; no custom assertion formats accepted for initial rollout
Decision 2025-02-21: Use 'actor_id' field as primary link between SAML subject and RBAC principal in audit schema
Decision 2025-02-25: Minimum evidence retention for acceptance = 30 days of sanitized logs + mapping diffs
